host: Apple M2 Max, 12 cores, 64 GB, numba 0.68 workqueue layer, 8 threads
question: Can a 5 ms slice of the whole MaleCNS graph finish in 4 ms, and does the whole graph behave?

whole_brain.retina: lamina L1/L2/L3 by ommatidium column (1767/1767/892 cells, 1768 hex features), light-decrement drive gain 2.0
whole_brain.within_4ms: median yes; worst blocks exceed 4 ms during strong whole-eye stimulation
whole_brain.behaviour_normalized_weights: inert past the lamina: motor neurons never fire (incoming |weight| per neuron normalised to 1.1 so a cell needs most inputs active at once)

behaviour_per_synapse_weights.model: weight = w_s * synapse_count * sign, no per-neuron normalisation; w_s = 1/25.5 of threshold (the ratio used by the published whole-brain LIF model; verify against Shiu et al. 2024 before citing numbers)
behaviour_per_synapse_weights.result: bistable: silent until any stimulus (even a 9-column dark spot), then ~1.2-1.9 % of neurons fire indefinitely with every motor channel saturated; never decays back; 4.3 ms median block (over budget)

sweep.cap_incoming_2_3_5_10: inert past lamina (cap 10 leaves a small local reverberation)

behaviour_per_synapse_weights.conclusion: a uniform point-neuron model of the whole connectome either does nothing or never stops; no stimulus-driven regime was found without inventing cell-specific parameters

live_slice.note: default; retina -> LC4/LPLC2 -> descending neurons -> VNC motor neurons; responds to dark/bright objects and the cursor

supervision_note: for the parallel kernel the main thread's CPU time under-measures compute, so the strict 4 ms check uses wall time (desktop_neural.py); for the numpy kernel it remains thread CPU time
sign_rule: consensus_nt: acetylcholine +1; gaba -1; glutamate -1 (assumption); modulatory, conflicting, or unclear excluded
raw_data: /tmp scratch scripts fb_engine.py and fb_persyn.py (not kept); numbers above are from runs on 2026-10-07
